newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Ifo May business sentiment.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Ifo May business sentiment.

text.p: Following are comments from economists on the Ifo economic research institute report.

Ifo said it expected German Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to grow two to 2.5 percent in 1997 and said it believed Germany would not meet budget deficit critierion for European monetary union, but this would not preclude it from qualifying.
Ifo also said its west German business climate index rose to 95.3 in May from 94.7 in April.
ARMIN KAYSER, ECONOMIST, SWISS BANK CORP, FRANKFURT:

"The numbers (business sentiment index) are a touch above expectations. There were rumours in the market for slightly higher data. The numbers support the view that the economic recovery is on track and that the economy is poised for expansion.

"I do not think there is much danger for inflation. The current recovery is unique in that we have the cost side, or wages, fixed for two years while the economy recovers. This is a favourable backdrop.
"I think it is still an export-led recovery and all of the numbers out for the moment show sectors related to exports doing well. But domestic markets are subdued.
"A wild card could be capital spending. There are signs that capital spending and demand for capital goods are picking up. That is one point of hope for domestic demand."
HANS-GUENTHER REDEKER, ECONOMIST, CHASE INVESTMENT BANK, LONDON:

"I was not surprised by 95.3 for west Germany. It's a good number. We are seeing an export-led recovery gaining strength. Yet capital goods orders are still disappointing which will keep the labour market under pressure.
MICHAEL HOCHGUERTEL, HEAD OF MONEY MARKETS; BHF-BANK, FRANKFURT:

"I strongly agree (with Redeker). In May there were many holidays and so-called bridge days. That usually leads to a lower figure. Fortunately that wasn't true this time. We are seeing an export-led recovery."
RALF KUGELSTADT, ECONOMIST, UBS GERMANY, FRANKFURT:
"The figures are pretty unspectacular and very much in line with expectations. We were expecting 95.0 (for May business sentiment) so it is bang in line with that.
"In theory, we could have expected some kind of consolidation in May because the fiscal situation with the Bundesbank asset revaluation and also because the dollar was weaker.

"A slight increase means that growth in the second quarter is secure and this is confirmed through Ifo. It is a good sign for capital investment growth and Ifo is usually a good indicator of capital investment."
